advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the reduced session-replay coverage in test_mcp_auth.py is acceptable given the mint-suppression guard, or add a coverage note.
evidence: tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py:428-431: replay uses `"Mcp-Session-Id": "forged-id"` and `bare` carries no session
Original test replayed the server-minted `session_id`; the new version cannot because none is minted
advisory.finding: The adapted auth test no longer exercises replaying a REAL minted session id against an authenticated principal; it only asserts no session is minted and that forged/bare unauthenticated requests get 401. If a future change makes the server stateful again, the `session_id is None` assertion will fail loudly (good), but until then the test provides weaker positive coverage of the actual hijack defense than before — it now proves absence of the artifact rather than resistance to its reuse.
scenarios: A regression re-enables per-session state but the mint-suppression check is separately relaxed

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider asserting statelessness also holds under the proxy-auth (auth_enabled + proxy strategy) HTTP configuration.
evidence: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:657: if auth_enabled and "proxy" in mcp_cfg.auth_strategies: ... rewraps streamable_http_app
stateless flag lives on the underlying session manager, which the proxy middleware wraps but does not replace, so the property should still hold — but it is untested under that config
advisory.finding: The stateless_http=True wiring in build_server is only exercised for the HTTP branch; there is no assertion or test that the proxy-auth middleware path (auth_enabled and 'proxy' in auth_strategies, which rewraps streamable_http_app) still yields a stateless session manager, since _http_server() in the new test uses allow_unauthenticated_http without proxy auth.
scenarios: A proxy-auth deployment where a refactor of the wrapping accidentally reintroduces stateful behavior

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the private `_session_manager.stateless` internal assertion with an observable behavioral check (e.g. a request carrying an unknown session id is served, no session id is minted).
evidence: The docstring admits the coupling: 'if this fails the SDK's internals moved and this test needs updating' (line 41-42)
Statelessness is already covered observably in test_mcp_auth.py:422 via `assert session_id is None`, so this internal-flag assertion adds coupling without adding observable coverage.
advisory.finding: The new test asserts the private SDK internal `srv._session_manager.stateless` flag rather than observable HTTP behavior; it is a change-detector that breaks on an SDK-internal reorganization with no observable-behavior change, as the test's own precondition message concedes ('if this fails the SDK's internals moved and this test needs updating').
scenarios: SDK renames `_session_manager` or moves the `stateless` flag in a behavior-preserving release upgrade.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the effective statelessness of the served app (observable no-session behavior) rather than the config value round-tripped on settings.
evidence: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:643: `stateless_http=True,` — the assertion reads back the literal value the same code path passed in.

The docstring itself says the risk it targets is 'a setting on a Settings object that never reaches FastMCP' — but reading `srv.settings.stateless_http` cannot distinguish a setting that reached the session manager from one that did not; only the session manager's effective behavior can.
advisory.finding: `test_the_stateless_setting_is_what_reaches_the_sdk` asserts `srv.settings.stateless_http is True`, which merely re-reads the kwarg the production line set on the same object; it is a change-detector on configuration state that would survive even if the SDK ignored the setting (the session manager could still be stateful), so it does not verify observable statelessness.
scenarios: A future SDK version accepts `stateless_http` on Settings but no longer wires it into StreamableHTTPSessionManager; this test stays green while the server is stateful.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that posts an authenticated INIT_REQUEST with an unknown Mcp-Session-Id and asserts it is served (200), not 404 'Session expired'.
evidence: tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py:429: `"/mcp", json=INIT_REQUEST, headers={**MCP_HEADERS, "Mcp-Session-Id": "forged-id"}` — no Authorization header, so line 433 `assert replay.status_code == 401` reflects auth refusal, not stateless session acceptance.
Ticket aca0-6a66-0a27-47cf acceptance criterion: 'Regression coverage asserts the chosen behaviour (session survival ...) across a simulated cutover.'

Named violating input: an INIT_REQUEST carrying a VALID bearer token AND a stale/unknown `Mcp-Session-Id` — under the old stateful code this 404s 'Session expired'; the added `stateless_http=True` (mcp_server.py:643) must make it return 200. No test drives this input.
ABSENCE: no test in tests/ posts a valid-token request with an unrecognized Mcp-Session-Id and asserts a 200 (served) response.
advisory.finding: No test exercises the actual bug symptom — a well-authenticated request carrying an orphaned/stale Mcp-Session-Id must now be SERVED (200) rather than 404'd 'Session expired'. The adapted auth test's forged-session request is refused at 401 by auth BEFORE any session lookup, so it never drives the stateless session-handling path the ticket's regression lives in.
scenarios: A future change reintroduces per-session state; a client whose container was swapped presents a valid token with a stale session id and gets 404 mid-task — exactly the reported bug — with no test to catch it.
